# AUDIT-PERF1000-2026-11-21: 1000 concurrent users who edit and recalculate

**Base:** `origin/main` 109b17b31 in the read-only worktree `F:\ecr-wt\audit-perf1000`.

**Method:**
- Code reading. Client inventory by one read-only sub-reviewer; I spot-checked its key lines.
- Arithmetic from real config values.
- Read-only Query Store and DMV queries on the stand database `EcrLandMsLegacy3`:
  - SQL Server 2022 Developer, 12 cores, max server memory 8000 MB, MAXDOP 6, cost threshold 5.
  - Instance up since 17.11 03:28. Query Store is READ_WRITE.
- One local micro-measurement: PBKDF2.

No code was changed, no tests were run, and the API, worker and load generators were not started. `EcrLegacyProd` was not touched.

Prior work treated as closed (not re-reported unless shown insufficient at 1000 users): `AUDIT-PSS-2026-11-20.md` (PSS-01…31) and `docs/build/HANDOVER-PSS-1121.md` §2.

**Evidence labels:**

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[code]** | Read in source (file:line, paths relative to `src/` unless stated). |
| **[QS]/[DMV]** | Measured on the stand. |
| **[calc]** | Arithmetic from the stated inputs. |
| **[UNVERIFIED]** | Plausible, with the measurement that would prove it. |

> ⚠ **Stand caveat.** Some Query Store rows come from stand binaries older than HEAD.
> - Example: query 8901 is the flat `StaleResultsQuery` form. HEAD replaced it with `StaleResultsByIdsQuery.PeriodDocuments` (`Ecr.Infrastructure/Persistence/StaleResultsMapCache.cs:660-685`), yet the stand still ran it until 21.11 16:33.
> - I use stand numbers only where they describe code that is unchanged in HEAD: the recalculation write path, the HSE400 loader, the queue, the purge. Everything else is marked [UNVERIFIED].
>
> The last yearly Land run (21.11 16:54:28–17:00:43, 30 doc×month runs) matches the brief's 6 m 49 s measurement.

---

## 1. Executive summary

**Verdict: No.** The current system will not serve 1000 concurrent users who start recalculations without hour-long waits. The HTTP tier and the polling load are fine. What breaks is calculation throughput:
- Methodology recalculation (the worker pool, SQL CPU and transaction log) breaks first.
- The interactive formula lane breaks second.

The safeguards added in the PSS pass work well at the scale of a single user. They cap and order the work but do not reduce how much of it there is.

**Bottleneck ranking (first to break):**

1. **Methodology recalculation throughput (PERF-01/02/03/05).**
   - One press of *Recalculate* on a year-layout (Land) document always recomputes **all open months** of the year (`RecalculateDocumentHandler.cs:329-348`). In November that is 11 months × 9–32 s per month (measured).
   - Measured cost per doc×month: **18.2 s of SQL CPU and 272 MB of transaction log**. 83 % of that log is calculation-step trace (insert plus purge).
   - Sustainable ceiling on the customer SQL (20 cores):
     - **≈ 2–3 document-years per minute** (120–180 per hour);
     - the log device limits it first at ~100 MB/s;
     - the 10 worker slots alone would allow ≈ 4.3.
   - Example demand: 300 active editors pressing once every 20 minutes = **15 per minute**, i.e. 5–7× the ceiling.
   - Because jobs merge by target, the backlog settles at roughly the number of documents involved (~250). The wait to start then grows to **≈ 1.5–3 hours**.
   - Until the recalculation runs, users **cannot submit**: stale results block submission (`Ecr.Application/Workflow/SubmitSheetHandler.cs:437-456`).
   - On top of this, a new press on a document whose year chain is running **restarts the chain from January** (PERF-02). The later months of busy documents may then never get computed during working hours.

2. **Interactive formula recalculation after each cell edit (PERF-04).**
   - Each API node runs **at most 5 formula jobs at once**: 1 reserved slot + 4 shared slots (`Ecr.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:440-454`, `Jobs/JobWorker.cs:30,42`).
   - A job averages **1.0 s** (stand, 883 jobs).
   - The ФВ-12.2 limit (< 10 s from edit to recalculation start) breaks above **≈ 75 editors typing at the same moment per API node**. With 300 such editors the wait is ≈ 55 s; with 1000 it is ≈ 3 min.
   - A running methodology step of the same document blocks formula jobs for another 9–32 s, because the claim skips that document.

3. **SQL concurrency (PERF-05).**
   - The PSS-02 cap of 4 applies **only to children of the yearly fan-out**.
   - Manual, automatic and cascade recalculations still run up to 10 jobs × 4 branches = **40 heavy sessions** per worker host.
   - The stand has already logged **22,845 THREADPOOL waits (longest 37.9 s)** and **708 RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE_QUERY_COMPILE waits (longest 300 s)** since 17.11.
   - On a 20-core SQL Server left at MAXDOP 0 (Resource Governor and the MAXDOP setting are optional, PSS-03), worker-thread exhaustion is likely.

4. **Cascade amplification from the HSE400 source document (PERF-06).** Every edit of HSE400 triggers its own recalculation (B179 L2b), and each of those then recalculates every consumer document × period. One wave on a 150-consumer, year-scoped setup is about 1,650 runs, i.e. **~40–75 minutes of the whole pool** [calc, consumer count UNVERIFIED].

5. **Sign-in behind NAT, RDS or a load balancer (PERF-07).**
   - `/api/v1/login/*`, Windows sign-in included, is limited to **60 per minute per client address** (`Ecr.Api/Security/LoginRateLimiting.cs:84,322-325`).
   - `TrustForwardedFor` is off by default.
   - If all 1000 users arrive from one address at 9:00, admitting them takes ≥ 17 minutes, with 429 responses meanwhile. This only matters on such a topology.

**Fine at 1000 users:**
- HTTP and polling: about 450 requests/s even in the bad scenario.
- Session and cookie validation (cached).
- The document list's staleness map (HEAD design).
- Memory grants on 32 GB.
- Scale-out of the API: no SignalR, keys in the database, recurring jobs under a distributed lock.

Details in §4.

**Top fixes (highest return first):**
1. **Recompute only the months whose inputs changed.** Reuse the D-562 input-change detection for manual year presses. Typical work per press drops about 11×.
2. **Stop the year chain from restarting** on absorption. Re-queue only the months that changed.
3. **Cut trace writes.** Either PSS-01 option 2 (no step trace for system runs; compute the explanation on demand), or bulk-copy plus compression.
4. **A global cap on heavy recalculation sessions**, sized from SQL cores, instead of a cap on fan-out children only.
5. **Make the interactive capacity configurable** and scale out API nodes.
6. **Show queue position and an estimated start time**, and back off polling while queued.

Items 1–3 need human decisions (§3).

**Counts:** Critical 1, High 6 (two of them conditional: PERF-06, PERF-07), Medium 6, Low 5 (18 findings).

## 2. Capacity model

### 2.1 Assumptions and sources

| # | Assumption | Source |

| A1 | 1000 concurrent sessions: 300 actively editing (typing or pasting), 600 viewing or reviewing a document, 100 on lists or admin pages. | Scenario of the brief; the 30/60/10 split is my assumption. |
| A2 | ~250 documents per year, so ~4 users per document. | PSS audit §6 item 13 (human). |

### 2.2 Methodology recalculation (recalc lane, worker pool)

**Service time:**
- Doc×month step S ≈ 12.7 s (median); largest document 32.3 s.
- Document-year = K × S = 11 × 12.7 ≈ **140 s** (typical) and 11 × 32.3 ≈ **355 s** (largest).

**Ceilings [calc]:**

| Limit | Formula | Doc×month per minute | Document-years per minute |
|---|---|---|---|
| Worker slots (10), if S does not grow from 4 to 10 concurrent [UNVERIFIED] | 10 × 60 / 12.7 | 47 | 4.3 |
| SQL CPU, all 20 cores given to recalculation | 20 × 60 / 18.2 | 66 | 6.0 |
| SQL CPU, half the cores left for interactive work | 10 × 60 / 18.2 | 33 | 3.0 |
| Log at 100 MB/s (A12) | 100 × 60 / 272 | **22** | **2.0** |
| Log at 200 MB/s | 200 × 60 / 272 | 44 | 4.0 |

**Effective capacity ≈ 2–3 document-years per minute.** The stand itself ran 4.8 doc×month/min at 21.6 MB/s of log, 4 jobs at a time.

**Demand:**
- One press on a year-layout document is one document-year (`RecalculateDocumentHandler.cs:329-348`). Jobs merge only per target `doc{id}-y{year}[-s{sheet}]`.
- Scenario: 300 editors, one press every 20 minutes each = **15 document-years/min**, so ρ ≈ 5–7.
- Lighter scenario: every one of the 250 documents recalculated once an hour = 4.2/min, still ρ > 1.
- Break-even: about 120–180 presses per hour across the whole system, roughly one press per document every 1.5–2 hours.

**Queue wait while saturated:**
- Merging by target bounds the backlog by the number of distinct targets, so the wait to start ≈ backlog ÷ throughput:
  - one target per document: 250 / 2.5 ≈ **100 min**;
  - one target per sheet scope (each sheet a separate target): 2–3× that.
- This is FIFO by `AvailableAt` (`DbJobQueue.cs:101-111`). The manual-first pass (`DbJobQueue.cs:139-142`) does not help, because every press is manual.

**After fix PERF-01** (recompute only months with changed inputs; a typical edit touches 1 month): work per press ≈ 1 step. Capacity becomes ≈ 22–33 presses/min, so ρ ≈ 0.5–0.7 and the start wait is tens of seconds.

### 2.3 Interactive formula lane (API process)

**Model:** a closed system. Each editor has at most one queued formula job, because jobs merge per (document, period, user) — `Ecr.Application/Documents/PatchCellsHandler.cs:3716-3727`.

**Inputs:** throughput X = 5 slots / 1.0 s = 5 jobs/s per API node; time between an editor's edits Z ≈ 5 s.

**Wait R = N/X − Z** for N simultaneously typing editors [calc]:

| N per node | Wait R |
|---|---|
| 75 | 10 s (ФВ-12.2 limit) |
| 150 | 25 s |
| 300 | 55 s |
| 1000 | 195 s |

**Extra blocking from the document claim rule:** a methodology step of the same document that is running blocks the claim (`DbJobQueue.cs:163-168`) for up to one step (9–32 s measured, 131 s observed earlier under contention: `doc3-year` at 07:04, 786 s for 6 steps).

**Client follow-up:** the client follows each formula job for at most 60 polls × 2 s = 120 s (`Ecr.Web/src/features/grid/useCellPatch.ts:121-128,194`). Above roughly 600 typing editors per node it stops following before the job runs. The grid observer takes over only if the grid is still mounted.

### 2.4 SQL sessions, threads and memory (worst case, one worker host)

**Heavy sessions:** 10 jobs × 4 branches = 40 (`Ecr.Calculations/CalculationOrchestrator.cs:223,239`), plus 5 formula jobs, 2 Excel jobs, and staleness-map loads.

**Worker threads:**
- A parallel query at DOP 4 typically reserves 2×DOP+1 ≈ 9 workers. 40 × 9 = 360, plus ≈ 250 API and worker sessions, gives ≈ **610 of 768**.
- At MAXDOP 0 (DOP up to 20): 40 × 41 ≫ 768, so THREADPOOL waits.

**Memory grants:**
- Workspace ≈ 0.75 × (max server memory ≈ 28 GB) ≈ 21 GB.
- 40 grants × 245 MB (largest seen in QS) ≈ 10 GB, which fits. Memory waits on the stand fell from 25,303 s (20.11) to 123 s (21.11).
- Buffer-pool churn from trace writes at saturation: 47 runs/min × 49 MB ≈ **2.3 GB/min** of new pages → page-life-expectancy pressure → PAGEIOLATCH on interactive reads.
  - Stand cumulative: `Ecr_hot` read 268 GB since 17.11 on a ~50 GB database; PAGEIOLATCH_SH 40,688 s.

**Connection pool:**
- API `Max Pool Size` 200 per node (`appsettings.json:14`).
- By Little's law, at ~450 req/s exhaustion starts once the average time a connection is held exceeds 0.44 s. That happens when SQL CPU saturates (2.2, 2.4), and then users get "Connect Timeout" or 503 `databaseBusy`.

### 2.5 HTTP and polling [calc from the client inventory]

**Per-user request rates (tab visible):**

| User state | Requests/min | What they are |
|---|---|---|
| Viewer with a document open, no job | ≈ 6 | My tasks every 30 s; sheet `changes` every 30 s; discussion summary every ~32 s |
| Editor | ≈ 48 | The 6 above + ~12 PATCH (one every 5 s) + 30 job polls (2 s follower) |
| Waiting for a manual recalculation | + ≈ 58 | Sheet follower every 1.5 s (`SheetActions.tsx:1126-1140`, `jobFollow.ts:7`) + My tasks switching to 3 s (`useMyTasks.ts:15,33`) |

**Scenario total:**
- 600 × 6 + 300 × 48 + 150 waiting × 58 ≈ **26,700 requests/min ≈ 445 requests/s**.
- About 40 % of that is job-status polling caused only by queue waits.
- Each authenticated request costs 2–4 small SQL statements:
  - security-stamp check (5 s cache, so effectively once per request at these intervals);
  - access profile (1–2 statements);
  - the handler itself.
- That is ≈ 1–2 k statements/s, which the server can carry at 20 cores [UNVERIFIED per-request CPU].

**Sheet change probe:** ≈ 2.5 k logical reads and 2–3 ms per call on the largest Land sheet (`Ecr.Infrastructure/Persistence/SheetChangeStore.cs:14-18`). 33 polls/s ≈ 83 k reads/s, which is acceptable.

### 2.6 Sign-in burst

**Local password:**
- PBKDF2-SHA512, 200,000 iterations (`Ecr.Infrastructure/Security/PasswordHasher.cs:20,36`).
- Measured cost: 96.6 ms (repo measurement, SHA-256 on .NET 10, `LoginRateLimiting.cs:58-60`) and 651 ms (my measurement, SHA-512 on .NET Framework 4.x on this PC; an upper bound).
- 1000 sign-ins = 100–650 CPU-seconds, i.e. 0.2–1.1 cores over a 10-minute burst. **Not a problem.**
- Windows (Kerberos) sign-in does not run PBKDF2.

**Rate limit** — the real constraint:
- 60 per minute per client address, applied to `/api/v1/login` and `/api/v1/login/windows` (`LoginRateLimiting.cs:92,322-325`).
- `TrustForwardedFor` = false (`appsettings.json:44`).
- The 30-minute idle sign-out (`Ecr.Application/Security/SessionSettingsHandlers.cs:28`) adds re-logins through the day.

## 3. Findings

### PERF-01: One *Recalculate* press always recomputes the whole open year

- **Area / severity:** Recalculation throughput. **Critical**: it is the first thing to break, and it blocks submission.
- **Evidence:**
  - **The press always means the whole year** for year-layout documents.
    - [code] `Ecr.Application/Documents/RecalculateDocumentHandler.cs:329-348`: payload `Year = scopeYear, PeriodKey = null`, target `YearScopedTargetOf`.
    - [code] `Ecr.Infrastructure/Jobs/RecalculationJob.cs:483-509`: a chain step takes the first period of the remaining scope; every open month is computed.
    - Skipping unchanged months exists only for the nightly run (`Jobs:NightlyRecalculation:SkipUnchanged`, `appsettings.json:76`; handover §2, PSS-15). The input-change detector is `Jobs/NightlyInputChangeQuery.cs`.
  - **Cost per month:** [QS] 18.2 s SQL CPU and 272 MB log (A5). [DMV] 9–32 s wall time per month (A4).
  - **Stale results block submission:** [code] `Ecr.Application/Workflow/SubmitSheetHandler.cs:437-456` (`ECR-SUB-4221.staleMethodologyResults`). Comment at `Ecr.Application/Calculations/CalculationTrigger.cs:13-14`.
  - **No estimated wait for the user:** [code] no queue position or ETA anywhere (grep for `QueuePosition|jobsAhead` finds 0 matches).
- **Failure scenario:** model in §2.2.
  - Demand of 15 document-years/min against capacity of 2–3/min. The start wait grows to ≈ 1.5–3 h by mid-day.
  - Users who edited one month cannot submit until 11 months are recomputed.
  - Near a deadline, submissions stall system-wide.
- **Proposed fix:** a *manual* year press recomputes only months whose inputs changed since that month's current run.
  - Reuse the D-562 detector (`NightlyInputChangeQuery`) per (document, month). Unchanged months keep their current run.
  - Always include the month on screen, so the user's "I pressed and nothing happened" stays honest.
  - Write a sheet-log entry "skipped unchanged". A **Force full** option needs `Calculation.Recalculate`.
  - Changes B59 (B24 behaviour is kept) and extends D-562 to manual presses.
- **Proof plan:**
  - Integration test `Ecr.Infrastructure.Tests/Jobs/YearPressSkipsUnchangedMonthsTests`: edit month 3 of an 11-month Land document, press, assert exactly 1 new `CalculationRun`; edit nothing, press, assert 0 runs plus the "nothing changed" outcome.
  - Stand: count `calc.CalculationRun` rows per press before and after, and the `CreatedAt→StartedAt` distribution under the load scenario in §5.
- **Effort:** M.
- **Needs human decision: yes.** May a manual year press skip months with unchanged inputs (D-562 extended, B59 amended)? Default proposal: yes, plus a "force full" for holders of `Calculation.Recalculate`.

### PERF-02: The year chain restarts from the first month whenever a new press arrives

- **Area / severity:** Recalculation throughput and fairness. **High**: wasted work grows with how busy a document is, and later months can starve.
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] `Ecr.Infrastructure/Jobs/DbJobQueue.cs:915-972` (`ContinueAsync`). At the end of a step, if a `Queued` row with the **same target** exists (`@behind`):
    - the running chain is set `Cancelled` ("absorbed");
    - the queued fresh job is revived (`RevivedAvailableAt`);
    - its payload has no chain fields, so it starts again from the first open month (`ChainResetTemplate` `:310-312`, H1 rationale `:305-309`).
  - [code] Presses merge into that `Queued` row (`EnqueueSql:404-460`).
  - [DMV] Restarts already happen on the stand: `doc3-year` started 07:04:41 and ran 1,080 s; the `doc4/5/6-year` rows of 07:01:55 were `Cancelled`.
- **Failure scenario:**
  - A document-year chain takes 11 × 12.7–32.3 s = 2.3–6 min of pure work, plus queue time between steps when the pool is busy.
  - Any press on the same target during that window restarts the year: January is recomputed again and December is reached only in a quiet window.
  - With 4 editors per document, each pressing about every 20 min, a press arrives on average every 5 min.
  - Result: the later months of busy documents stay stale all day, while January is computed many times.
- **Proposed fix:** on absorption, keep the chain's progress.
  - Continue with the remaining months.
  - Append only the already-done months whose inputs changed after their step started. The PERF-01 detector supplies these, or the `aud.CellChange` predicate `ChangedAt > run.StartedAt` that `StaleResultsByIdsQuery` already uses.
  - Preserves the H1 correctness goal ("the change may have touched done months") without redoing unchanged months.
- **Proof plan:**
  - `DbJobQueueChainAbsorbKeepsProgressTests`: 6-step chain; press after step 2 touching month 5 only. Expect remaining months 3–6 plus none redone.
  - Press touching month 1, expect month 1 appended once.
  - Stand: runs per doc×month per hour under the load scenario.
- **Effort:** M.
- **Needs human decision: yes.** Is "redo only changed done months" an acceptable reading of H1 (review of PSS-04)?

### PERF-03: Calculation-step trace dominates write volume (log and buffer-pool churn)

- **Area / severity:** SQL throughput. **High**: the log device becomes the first hard limit (§2.2), and buffer-pool churn slows interactive reads.
- **Evidence:**
  - **Log volume:** [QS] for the 30-run yearly run, the log total was 8,147 MB.
    - EF `MERGE … calc.CalculationStep` (query 2511): 3,507 MB.
    - Purge `DELETE TOP … calc.CalculationStep` (query 9013): 3,203 MB.
    - So **83 %** of the log is trace.
  - **Steps go row by row through EF batches:** 21,435 statements per 30 runs ≈ **715 round trips per run** (query 2511). Results already use bulk copy (query 2499).
  - **Rows and storage per run:** [DMV] ≈ 12.6 k step rows per run, ≈ 3.9 KB each (46,107 MB / 11.7 M rows, of which 10,078 MB is LOB `TraceJson`). The table is uncompressed (PSS-01).
  - **Retention** keeps only the current chain (D-560). That limits stored volume, but every recalculation still writes about 49 MB of trace and then deletes the previous run's 49 MB: about 100 MB of churn per doc×month.
  - **Projected size** of Current trace at customer volume: 3,000 doc×months × 49 MB ≈ **150 GB per year** for Land-sized documents [calc; document size UNVERIFIED].
- **Failure scenario:**
  - At 22–47 runs/min, the log write rate is 100–210 MB/s (A12). Commit latency (WRITELOG; stand cumulative 17,579 s) rises for everyone, PATCH included.
  - In FULL recovery, log backups must carry 6–13 GB per hour of recalculation alone.
  - Trace pages push hot `doc.CellValue` and result pages out of the buffer pool.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - (a) **PSS-01 option 2.** Persist step trace only when the user asks for an explanation (re-compute on demand), or only for runs that become Current for a submitted sheet. This was not adopted in the PSS pass, and the human chose purge (§6 item 1).
  - (b) If trace must stay:
    - insert steps with `SqlBulkCopy` or a TVP, as results are;
    - store `TraceJson` with `COMPRESS()` or as a compact binary;
    - PAGE-compress the partitions after the first purge (handover §4 item 2).
  - (c) Write trace **outside** the document lock, after the run switch, so other jobs of the document are not held up.
- **Proof plan:**
  - [QS] `avg_log_bytes_used × count_executions` per run (query in §5.1), before and after.
  - `sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats` on the log file, delta over a single yearly run.
  - Integration test: one run writes ≤ N step rows (option a) or uses one bulk copy (option b).
- **Effort:** M (b), L (a).
- **Needs human decision: yes.** Is a persisted step trace required for every automatic or manual run, or may it be produced on demand (ЗБР-1 / D-560 trace policy)?

### PERF-04: Interactive formula lane capacity is 5 jobs per API node

- **Area / severity:** Interactive latency. **High**: ФВ-12.2 (< 10 s) is missed above about 75 editors typing at once per node.
- **Evidence:**
  - **Slots:** [code] API worker lanes `interactive, default, excel` (`Ecr.Infrastructure/Jobs/JobLaneMap.cs:106-109`). `MaxConcurrency` 4 shared (`JobWorker.cs:30`), `ReservedConcurrency` 1 (`:42`). Neither is configurable for the API (`DependencyInjection.cs:440-454` sets neither).
  - **Each autosave enqueues a formula job** (`PatchCellsHandler.cs:222-285, 3716`). Jobs merge per (document, period, **user**) via `FormulaRecalculationTarget.Of`.
  - **Formula jobs take the document lock** (`FormulaRecalculationJob.cs:121-123`).
  - **The claim skips documents with a running job** in recalc or interactive (`DbJobQueue.cs:163-168`).
  - [DMV] mean job time 1.0 s, max 10.1 s; mean wait 9.0 s, max 245.5 s on a 1–3-user stand.
  - **Client:** follows for 120 s at most (`useCellPatch.ts:121-128`); polls `GET /jobs/{id}` every 2 s (`:399`, inventory).
- **Failure scenario** (§2.3): 300 editors typing on one node see derived columns update after ≈ 55 s; with 1000, ≈ 3 min. During a methodology step of the same document, add up to one step (9–32 s).
- **Proposed fix:**
  - (1) Configurable `Jobs:Interactive:Concurrency` (reserved interactive slots), default 4. Separate from `default`, so long collections do not take them.
  - (2) Measure the CPU of a formula job. If it is mostly SQL wait, raise the concurrency; if it is CPU, add API nodes. The JobWorker in each API node then adds capacity linearly; the API is scale-out safe (§4).
  - (3) Let the claim take a formula job for a document whose methodology step is between its formula and methodology phases [UNVERIFIED feasibility]. Otherwise keep the step short (PERF-01).
  - (4) Client: show "queued for recalculation (N ahead)" instead of silently stopping the follower at 120 s.
- **Proof plan:**
  - Load test §5.2 "editors" profile. Measure the distribution of formula job `CreatedAt→StartedAt` from `itg.JobProgress` (query in §5.1): p95 < 10 s at the target number of editors per node.
  - Unit test: options binding for the new key.
- **Effort:** S (config) / M (claim change).
- **Needs human decision: no** for the config. Yes if API scale-out (2+ nodes) is to become the default topology (D-32).

### PERF-05: Heavy recalculation concurrency is not capped for manual, automatic and cascade jobs

- **Area / severity:** SQL stability. **High**: the PSS-02 fix does not hold at 1000 users.
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] The cap applies only to `FanOutParentJobId IS NOT NULL` plus cascades while a schedule is active (`DbJobQueue.cs:196-217`). Everything else is claimed by every free child (10, `worker.settings.json:8`).
  - [code] Each job runs 4 branches with their own DbContext (`CalculationOrchestrator.cs:223,239`). A second worker host doubles everything (no global count).
  - [DMV] cumulative since 17.11 on the stand (12 cores, 640 workers):
    - THREADPOOL: 22,845 waits, longest 37.9 s;
    - RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE_QUERY_COMPILE: 708 waits, 14,546 s, longest 300 s;
    - CXCONSUMER: 59,568 s;
    - stand MAXDOP 6, cost threshold 5.
  - [QS] Memory waits fell to 123 s on 21.11 (a single yearly run, fan-out cap 4). The PSS fix works only while concurrency stays at 4.
  - Resource Governor and MAXDOP stay optional (PSS-03 human decision 3; `Sql/16-resource-governor.sql`).
- **Failure scenario:**
  - At 1000 users all 10 children run manual presses, so 40 heavy sessions.
  - At MAXDOP 4: ≈ 610 of 768 worker threads (§2.4).
  - At the SQL Server default MAXDOP 0 on 20 cores: THREADPOOL waits. The API's `GET` requests then cannot obtain a worker, and logins and health checks time out.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - Global cap on **all** Running recalc-lane jobs, via the existing applock prologue and a second count: `Jobs:Recalculation:MaxConcurrency`. Default `max(2, SQL cores/4)`, which is 5 on 20 cores.
  - Under it, keep "manual first, fan-out ≤ 4".
  - Default `Calculations:MaxParallelism` = 2 for the worker profile.
  - Startup warning when `Count × MaxParallelism × (instance MAXDOP or cores)` exceeds 0.5 × max worker threads. `SqlCapabilitiesProbe` can read `sys.dm_os_sys_info.max_workers_count`.
  - Make the install guide's MAXDOP 4 / cost threshold 50 **required** for profiles of more than 200 users.
  - Changes PSS-02 / D-561 and PSS-03 (RG and MAXDOP optional).
- **Proof plan:**
  - `RecalcLaneGlobalCapDbTests`: 12 manual jobs, 10 claimers, so ≤ 5 Running.
  - Stand: 10 manual presses at once. Before and after: THREADPOOL and RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE deltas (§5.1), and `GET` document p95 from the sampler.
- **Effort:** M.
- **Needs human decision: yes.** (1) Global recalculation concurrency default. (2) Should MAXDOP and cost threshold become mandatory installer checks for large profiles (revisits PSS-03 item 3)?

### PERF-06: An HSE400 source edit fans out to every consumer document × period

- **Area / severity:** Recalculation throughput. **High** (conditional on how many consumers there are and how often HSE400 is edited).
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] `Ecr.Infrastructure/Jobs/SourceDocumentChangeHook.cs:73-81,170-183`. B179 L2b ("trigger on every source edit", human Q1): each edit of the source document queues the source's own `-auto` recalculation. On success, `:196-212` queues `RegistryImpactRecalculationJob` for (binding, year, month). Month = 0, i.e. the **whole year**, when the project is not monthly (`:189`).
  - [code] `RegistryImpactRecalculationJob.cs:61-67,94-110`: all consumers × periods → `RequestDependentsAsync` (10 s debounce, `CalculationTrigger.cs:174`).
  - The cascade cap applies only while a project schedule is active (`DbJobQueue.cs:192-195`).
  - [DMV] the stand shows this pattern: `doc3..6-p202604..07-dependent` rows at 06:54–06:58.
- **Failure scenario** [calc; customer consumer count UNVERIFIED]:
  - With 150 Land consumers in a year-scoped source: one HSE400 recalculation → 150 × 11 = 1,650 runs ≈ 1,650 × 18.2 s = 8.3 h of SQL CPU, or **38–75 min of the whole pool**.
  - HSE400 editors work all day, so a new wave merges into the still-queued targets. The pool stays saturated by cascades.
  - Manual presses overtake cascades (manual-first pass), but every slot is busy with 10–30 s cascade steps. Log and CPU load (PERF-03, -05) persist.
  - With a monthly source: 150 runs per wave, still about 3–7 min of the pool for each edit burst.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - (1) Recompute a consumer only if the source rows it actually reads changed. The loader can compare the HSE400 composition fingerprint (see PERF-11) with the one stored on the consumer's current run.
  - (2) Collapse consumer waves to at most one per binding×year per N minutes (configurable), not per source run.
  - (3) Alternatively, trigger consumers on Submit/Approve of the source month, not on every edit. The ApprovedOnly gate already does this for `ApprovedOnly`.
- **Proof plan:**
  - Query: number of consumer documents per binding×year on customer-like data.
  - Test `SourceEditCascadeCollapsesTests`: 5 source edits in 2 min → ≤ 1 consumer wave; a source edit that does not change composition → 0 consumer runs.
- **Effort:** M.
- **Needs human decision: yes.** Revisit B179 L2b Q1 ("trigger on every source edit") and the PSS-07 ≤ 15 s debounce for *source-document* cascades.

### PERF-07: The sign-in rate limit is per client address, Windows sign-in included

- **Area / severity:** Authentication. **High** if users reach the API through NAT, a reverse proxy or load balancer, or RDS/Citrix; otherwise Low.
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] `Ecr.Api/Security/LoginRateLimiting.cs:84` (60/min); `:92` (prefix `/api/v1/login` covers `login/local` and `login/windows`); `:322-325` (key = client address); `:391-400` (fixed window, `QueueLimit = 0`).
  - `ForwardedClientAddress.cs:12-19,117-119`: socket address unless `TrustForwardedFor`. Default false, `appsettings.json:44-45`.
  - Handover §6: "behind NAT without `TrustForwardedFor` all users are one address".
  - Idle sign-out after 30 min (`SessionSettingsHandlers.cs:28`).
- **Failure scenario:** 1000 users behind one address at 9:00.
  - The first 60 sign-ins each minute pass; the rest get 429 `ECR-AUTH-0429`.
  - Admitting everyone takes ≥ 17 min.
  - The same happens after lunch, when idle sessions expire together.
  - The Kerberos sign-in does no PBKDF2 at all, yet it consumes the same quota.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - (1) Separate partition for `login/windows`: the request is already Negotiate-authenticated, and its DB cost is one user lookup. Give it a high limit (e.g. 600/min per address) or a per-SID limit.
  - (2) For `login/local`, a per-(address + user name) partition with a modest per-address ceiling (e.g. 300/min). Account lockout (ФВ-6.4a) stays the credential guard.
  - (3) The installer asks for the topology (proxy, LB, RDS) and writes `TrustForwardedFor` and `KnownProxies`.
- **Proof plan:**
  - `Ecr.Api.Tests/Security/LoginRateLimitTopologyTests`: 120 Windows sign-ins from one address in a minute → 0 × 429; 61 failed local sign-ins with one user name from one address → 429.
  - Stand: k6 sign-in burst (§5.2).
- **Effort:** S.
- **Needs human decision: yes.** Customer network topology (direct, NAT, proxy, RDS), and whether Windows sign-in may get a separate limit.

### PERF-08: Polling stays at full rate while a job waits in the queue

- **Area / severity:** HTTP load and client. **Medium**: it amplifies saturation; it is not a root cause.
- **Evidence (client inventory, verified spot lines):**
  - My tasks polls every 3 s while one of the user's own non-formula jobs is Queued (`features/jobs/useMyTasks.ts:15,33,54-59`).
  - The manual sheet recalculation polls every 1.5 s while Queued (`SheetActions.tsx:1126-1140`, `jobFollow.ts:7,49-51`).
  - The project recalculation banner polls every 3 s.
  - No backoff on 5xx or 429 for the `changes` poll, chat or My tasks (`useSheetChanges.ts:110-114`).
  - TanStack retries 5xx twice with no jitter and ignore `Retry-After` (`app/queryClient.ts:53-57`).
  - The My tasks and `changes` timers have no jitter.
- **Failure scenario:** with 1-hour queue waits (PERF-01), 150 waiting users produce ≈ 145 polls/s of `GET /jobs` while nothing changes (§2.5). On a 5xx storm, 1000 clients retry together after 1 s and then 2 s.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - While `Queued`, poll at an interval that grows with queue position (e.g. 3 s → 30 s); once `Running`, poll every 2 s.
  - Add ±20 % jitter to every interval.
  - Honour `Retry-After` and back off exponentially on 5xx and 429 for all pollers.
  - Return `queuePosition` and an ETA in `GET /jobs/{id}` (see PERF-10).
- **Proof plan:** vitest for the interval function; k6 counts of `/jobs` requests per waiting user before and after.
- **Effort:** S–M.
- **Needs human decision: no.**

### PERF-09: Grid refetch fan-out after job completion and after other users' status changes

- **Area / severity:** API CPU and client. **Medium** [cost UNVERIFIED].
- **Evidence:**
  - [code, client]
    - On formula job completion, `invalidateSlicesForPeriods` refetches **every mounted visible slice** of the document in the written periods (`features/grid/sliceCache.ts:90-127`, `useCellPatch.ts:90-119`).
    - Another user's status transition makes every viewer refetch all visible slices plus five other queries (`SheetLiveRefresh.tsx:212-241`, `refreshSheetWorkflow.ts:22-28`).
    - `structuralSharing:false` (`sliceCachePolicy.ts:23-34`) means each refetch rebuilds every row model. That is ~30 k cells through `editorValueOf` (`gridRowModels.ts:147-173`).
  - [code, server] A slice `GET` makes ≈ 20–25 sequential round trips (`Ecr.Application/Documents/GetTableSliceHandler.cs:165-515`) and returns all cells plus per-cell permissions, confirmations, formats and styles (≈ 77 k permission keys on the Land sheet, `sliceCachePolicy.ts:27-31`).
  - No ETag or 304 on the slice.
- **Failure scenario:**
  - 300 editors, each with a formula job every ~20 s, × V visible slices (≈ 3) ≈ 45 slice `GET`s/s.
  - At an assumed 50–150 ms CPU each [UNVERIFIED], that is 2–7 API cores, plus ≈ 1 k SQL round trips/s.
  - On top of this, an approval on a popular sheet refetches all slices for every viewer.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - (1) A cheap rowversion check before building the slice: return 304 with an ETag built from `MIN_ACTIVE_ROWVERSION` and the slice's max `RowVersion`, as `SheetChangeStore` already computes.
  - (2) Refetch only slices whose tables were written: the job already knows `writtenPeriods`; add `writtenTables`.
  - (3) Re-enable structural sharing for unchanged rows (keyed by `RowVersion`).
- **Proof plan:**
  - Measure slice `GET` CPU and SQL time on the largest Land table (Application Insights or OTel `Telemetry:Enabled`, or `dotnet-counters` plus Query Store per correlation).
  - Playwright trace for the full-rebuild time.
  - k6 profile §5.2.
- **Effort:** M.
- **Needs human decision: no.**

### PERF-10: No queue position, ETA or per-user fairness in the recalculation lane

- **Area / severity:** UX and fairness. **Medium**.
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] The claim is FIFO by `AvailableAt, JobId` (`DbJobQueue.cs:101-111`).
  - The manual-first pass is the same for every user (`:139-142`).
  - Per-user limit: 30 presses/min per **node** (`DocumentRecalculateQuota.cs:46-50`, in-memory, `:30`).
  - Chain steps keep their FIFO place (`DbJobQueue.cs:960-962`).
  - No position or ETA in any DTO (grep).
- **Failure scenario:**
  - One user pressing on 30 documents within a minute puts 30 document-years (≈ 30 × 140 s ÷ 10 slots ≈ 7 min of the whole pool) ahead of everyone else.
  - Waiting users see only "Queued" for an hour and press again, which merges harmlessly but adds polling.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - `queuePosition` and `estimatedStartUtc` in `JobStatus`. Position comes from `IX_JobProgress_Claim` via COUNT of eligible rows ahead; the ETA from a rolling mean step time.
  - Optional per-user round-robin in the manual pass: order by each user's queued-job rank.
- **Proof plan:** API test for the position field; DB test showing two users with 5 and 1 queued jobs alternate.
- **Effort:** M.
- **Needs human decision: yes.** Per-user fairness deviates from FIFO (D-232 / D-473 / D-561).

### PERF-11: The HSE400 composition is re-read from scratch by every Land doc×month run

- **Area / severity:** SQL CPU. **Medium**.
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] `Ecr.Infrastructure/Persistence/Hse400CompositionSnapshotLoader.cs:59-80,169-176`. Every registry snapshot that contains the composition registry reads the HSE400 cells across all periods of the chosen documents.
    - The predicates are `PeriodKey IN (20 params)`, `TableDefId IN (10)`, `ColumnDefId IN (≈ 80)`.
    - Cells are not narrowed to the chosen instances.
    - No cache across runs (the PSS-08 cache is per run).
  - [QS] query 4794:
    - 1,130 executions, mean **1.59 s CPU** and 1.79 s duration at DOP 6, only 4.6 k reads (CPU-bound on the large IN lists);
    - 91 executions in the 30-run yearly hour = 92.5 s CPU, about 17 % of that run's SQL CPU.
- **Failure scenario:** at 33–47 runs/min this is 0.9–1.2 cores of constant parallel load, with parallel bursts. It grows with the number of HSE400 documents and years.
- **Proposed fix:**
  - Process-level cache of the HSE400 overlay, keyed by (binding, the chosen HSE400 instance ids, the source's Current-run ids, and the max `RowVersion` of those instances' rows).
  - Narrow the cell read to the chosen instances' `TableRowId`s, or join `doc.TableRow` by instance.
- **Proof plan:**
  - Query Store execution count of query 4794 per yearly run: from 1 per doc×month to 1 per HSE400 change.
  - `Hse400CompositionCacheTests` (equivalence plus invalidation on a source edit).
- **Effort:** M.
- **Needs human decision: no.**

### PERF-12: Default configuration runs recalculations inside the API under Quartz

- **Area / severity:** Deployment. **Medium**.
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] `appsettings.json:81-83,90-93`: `Jobs:Queue:Mode = Quartz`, `Recalculation:Executor = InProcess`. `DbBackgroundJobScheduler.cs:70-77` defaults to Quartz.
  - Only `deploy-ecr.ps1` switches to Database + Worker when the worker service is installed (`tools/deploy-ecr.ps1:363,1159-1169`).
  - In Quartz mode:
    - the month chain, the fan-out cap and claim-time document exclusion do not exist (handover §6);
    - 16 threads are shared by all jobs (`QuartzJobTypeLimiter.cs:52`, `appsettings.json:85`);
    - jobs are lost on restart (`DependencyInjection.cs:387-393`).
- **Failure scenario:** a site installed with `-DisableWorker`, or an upgrade that loses the service environment, runs every recalculation in the API process. CPU and memory then compete with HTTP, and PERF-01's waits double.
- **Proposed fix:** in Production, warn at startup (degraded `/health/ready` note) when Mode = Quartz and Executor = InProcess. The installer refuses a "large" profile without the worker.
- **Proof plan:** `EcrConfigurationValidationTests` case; `ci-msi-install.ps1` assertion already exists for the worker path.
- **Effort:** S.
- **Needs human decision: yes.** Is a deployment without the worker acceptable for production at all?

### PERF-13: Excel lane (2 per node) and import preview gate (2 + queue of 4) at period-end

- **Area / severity:** Throughput. **Medium** [durations UNVERIFIED].
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] `Jobs:Excel:MaxConcurrency` 2 (`appsettings.json:78-80`, `JobLaneMap.cs:127`).
  - `ImportPreviewConcurrency` 2, `QueueLimit` 4 (`appsettings.json:47-48`).
  - Import apply has priority over exports (`JobLaneMap.cs:96-97`).
  - Exports limited to 6/min per user (`appsettings.json:60`).
- **Failure scenario:** 200 users export at a deadline. At an assumed 20 s per export: 200 × 20 / 2 ≈ 33 min until the last export; import previews beyond 6 waiting get 429.
- **Proposed fix:** measure export and import durations on Land; make the gate configurable per profile; run Excel jobs in the worker pool with their own slots.
- **Proof plan:** `itg.JobProgress` durations for `IExcelExportJob` and `IExcelImportJob` on the stand (query in §5.1); k6 burst of 50 exports.
- **Effort:** S–M.
- **Needs human decision: no.**

### PERF-14: Per-request role-assignment read is a full clustered scan

- **Area / severity:** SQL. **Low** (grows linearly with all role assignments).
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] `Ecr.Infrastructure/Security/AccessDecisionService.cs:52-68`: `a.UserId == userId || (PrincipalSid != null && groupSids.Contains(...))`, `OrderByDescending(Id)`, `Take(200)`, on every `BuildProfileAsync` (≈ 100 call sites).
  - `GroupsFingerprintAsync` (`:181-211`) adds a second query for Windows users with role-bearing groups.
  - [DMV] `PK_RoleAssignment`: 21,393 scans, 0 seeks; `UQ_RoleAssignment_User`: 10 seeks.
- **Failure scenario:** 1000 users × ~5 assignments = 5 k rows (≈ 60 pages) scanned per authenticated request. At 450 req/s that is ≈ 27 k reads/s and ≈ 0.2 cores. Not critical.
- **Proposed fix:** rewrite as `UNION ALL` of the two filtered seeks (`UQ_RoleAssignment_User`, `UQ_RoleAssignment_Sid`), then order and take 200 in the outer query.
- **Proof plan:** `SET STATISTICS IO` before and after on 5 k assignments; index usage seeks > 0.
- **Effort:** S.
- **Needs human decision: no.**

### PERF-15: "My tasks" walks every routine formula job of the user

- **Area / severity:** SQL. **Low**.
- **Evidence:**
  - [code] `Ecr.Infrastructure/Persistence/JobProgressStore.cs:437-459,481-499`: the `HideRoutine` and `HideChildren` filters sit inside the `CreatedByUserId, UpdatedAt DESC` range.
  - `FanOutParentJobId` is not in the index's INCLUDE ([DMV] `IX_JobProgress_CreatedBy_UpdatedAt` INCLUDE `State, JobCode`).
  - 30-day history purge (PSS audit §4).
  - At ~1 formula job per edit burst, an editor accumulates thousands of `Succeeded` formula rows.
- **Failure scenario:** ~10⁴ index rows per poll × 33 polls/s. Low, but it grows with retention.
- **Proposed fix:** purge `Succeeded` formula jobs after 24 h, or a filtered index `WHERE NOT (JobCode = formula AND State = 'Succeeded')`.
- **Proof plan:** STATISTICS IO with 20 k routine rows for one user.
- **Effort:** S (needs a migration token if it is an index).
- **Needs human decision: no** (purge horizon: 24 h proposed).

### PERF-16: Client long-session and synchronised-load details

- **Area / severity:** Client. **Low**.
- **Evidence (inventory):**
  - Tables in a sheet are never unmounted while the user stays on it: up to 91 RevoGrid instances, each holding a full slice (`SheetTables.tsx:190-199`).
  - `pendingRecalculations` entries are removed only when the job settles (`useCellPatch.ts:43-72`).
  - When a period reopen expires, every viewer refetches `slices.all()` at the same wall-clock moment (`features/documents/periodReopen/useDocumentPeriodReopen.tsx:72-82`, verified).
  - `refetchOnReconnect` is left at its default (on), so a VPN flap refetches everything for all affected users.
  - The import follower does not pause in hidden tabs (`followImportJob.ts:57-101`).
- **Proposed fix:**
  - Unmount off-screen grids after N (e.g. 10) mounted.
  - Add a random 0–30 s spread to the reopen-expiry timer.
  - Cap or prune `pendingRecalculations`.
  - Pause the import follower when the tab is hidden.
- **Proof plan:** Chrome heap snapshot after 2 h on a 91-table sheet; vitest for the timer spread.
- **Effort:** S–M.
- **Needs human decision: no.**

### PERF-17: In-memory limits and caches multiply with API nodes

- **Area / severity:** Scale-out. **Low**.
- **Evidence:** [code]
  - `DocumentRecalculateQuota` is in-memory per node (`Ecr.Api/Security/DocumentRecalculateQuota.cs:30`).
  - The ASP.NET rate limiter is per process.
  - `ImportPreviewGate` and the script-run concurrency limit are per node.
  - `StaleCountsEpoch` dirty marks are per process: other nodes see a PATCH within ≤ 15 s TTL, as documented in `StaleResultsMapCache.cs:52-61`.
  - `StaleMapWarmService` runs on every node (`Program.cs:179-181`).
- **Failure scenario:** with N nodes behind a round-robin load balancer, every limit is effectively ×N and every warm query runs N times. Correctness holds.
- **Proposed fix:** document the factor in the runbook; optionally move the recalculation quota to a DB counter.
- **Proof plan:** two-node stand test.
- **Effort:** S.
- **Needs human decision: no.**

### PERF-18: Interactive queries pay EF parameter-list compile variety

- **Area / severity:** SQL compile. **Low** [UNVERIFIED impact].
- **Evidence:**
  - [QS] 72,086 compiles over 2,069 statements in 30 h (1,930 s compile time).
  - Statements carry up to 220–400 parameters (e.g. `@p220`, `@p380`), from EF batched inserts and `Contains` lists.
  - RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE_QUERY_COMPILE: 708 waits / 14,546 s cumulative.
  - Most compiles are bulk insert (`insert bulk`, 5,746) and EF batch-size variants.
- **Failure scenario:** under 1000 users, more concurrent large compiles can queue at the compile memory gateway (waits up to 300 s were seen).
- **Proposed fix:**
  - Bulk-copy the remaining EF batch inserts (PERF-03b).
  - Use EF's `TranslateParameterizedCollectionsToConstants` only where a list is small and fixed; prefer TVPs or `OPENJSON` for long `Contains` lists in hot paths.
- **Proof plan:** compile counts in Query Store before and after; `sys.dm_exec_query_optimizer_info`.
- **Effort:** S–M.
- **Needs human decision: no.**

## 4. Checked and found fine (coverage)

**Request path:**
- No sync-over-async in `src`.
  - The only blocking call is `Thread.Sleep` in the worker child stub (`Ecr.Worker/ChildStub.cs:83`).
  - `OPTION (RECOMPILE)` appears only in version migration (`DocumentVersionMigrationStore.cs`) and in audit sort by display name (`AuditPaging.cs:127`).
- Security stamp is cached for 5 s per node (`Ecr.Infrastructure/Security/SecurityStampValidator.cs:24-91`); the cache only speeds up agreement.
- Idle-timeout policy is cached for 30 s (`IdleTimeoutPolicy.cs:24`).
- The cookie carries only group SIDs that have role assignments (`LoginHandler.cs:17-22`).
- The access profile is cached and keyed by user + stamp + group/assignment fingerprint (`AccessDecisionService.cs:42-111`), so it is safe across nodes.
- `SessionUserMiddleware` is CPU-only.

**Scale-out:**
- No SignalR or WebSocket, hence no sticky sessions or backplane needed.
- Data Protection keys are in the database, protected by certificate (`AuthenticationSetup.cs:274-330`).
- Recurring jobs take a SQL distributed lock (`QuartzJobAdapter.cs:125-130`, `RecurringScheduleService.cs:752`).
- Each node's JobWorker claims atomically with `READPAST` (`DbJobQueue.cs:101-119`).

**Database queue:**
- One lane per claim with index-ordered `TOP(1)`.
- The fan-out applock is held for milliseconds.
- The claim excludes busy documents through the filtered index `IX_JobProgress_Document_Active` (21,259 seeks).
- Merging by target uses `UX_JobProgress_Target_Queued`.
- [DMV] row lock waits on `itg.JobProgress` are negligible (13).

**Staleness map (HEAD):**
- Period map with single-flight, SWR, dirty-document healing and run-switch healing (`StaleResultsMapCache.cs:11-75`).
- The full load uses the `PeriodDocuments` form (≈ 2.3 k reads, 43–49 ms per the code's own note).
- The stand's query 8901 (flat form, 1.2–1.6 s CPU, 174 executions per idle hour) comes from older stand binaries. **Re-measure after deploying HEAD** (query in §5.1).

**Sheet change poll:** ≈ 2.5 k reads, 2–3 ms (`SheetChangeStore.cs:14-18`). The ETag saves only bandwidth, which is fine at ≈ 33 polls/s.

**Memory grants on 32 GB:** see §2.4. Memory waits on 21.11 were 123 s (20.11: 25,303 s), which shows PSS-02 and PSS-08 working at current concurrency.

**Lock waits on result inserts:**
- [QS] `insert bulk calc.CalculationResult` waited 4,168 s in the 06:00 interval of 21.11, but only **0.1 s for 429 executions** in the latest yearly run (16:00).
- Escalation counters on `calc.*` show 0 promotions after the 21.11 rebuild.
- Not reproducible on HEAD-like code. Keep the §5.1 lock query in the load test.

**Response compression:** on, HTTPS, level Fastest (`Ecr.Api/Program.cs:223-233`).

**Approval queue:** bounded scan of at most 1,000 submitted sheets (`ListMyApprovalQueueHandler.cs:46-52`).

**Rate limits for recalculation and export:** present, per user (they multiply per node, PERF-17).

**Client:**
- No interval or listener leaks (inventory §6).
- No `invalidateQueries()` without a filter.
- Session keep-alive only after real user activity, at most once per 30 s across tabs.
- Hidden tabs pause TanStack intervals and the formula follower.
- Bundle budget: route ≤ 250 KB, dynamic chunks ≤ 190 KB, Monaco ≤ 820 KB (`scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs`); no `dist` in the worktree to re-measure.

**PBKDF2 cost:** see §2.6. Not a bottleneck.

**HTTP volume:** ≈ 100 req/s in steady state with a document open (1000 × 6/min), and ≈ 450 req/s in the saturated scenario. ASP.NET and SQL can carry it if PERF-05 keeps SQL out of saturation.

## 5. Measurement kit

### 5.1 Read-only SQL (stand or customer copy; each < 30 s)

```sql
-- (1) SQL CPU, duration and LOG BYTES per hour (recalculation cost; PERF-01/03). Divide by runs in the window.
SELECT i.start_time,
  CAST(SUM(rs.avg_cpu_time*rs.count_executions)/1e6 AS decimal(12,1)) cpu_s,
  CAST(SUM(rs.avg_log_bytes_used*rs.count_executions)/1048576 AS decimal(12,1)) log_mb,
  SUM(rs.count_executions) execs
FROM sys.query_store_runtime_stats rs
JOIN sys.query_store_runtime_stats_interval i ON i.runtime_stats_interval_id = rs.runtime_stats_interval_id
WHERE i.start_time >= DATEADD(hour,-6,SYSUTCDATETIME())
GROUP BY i.start_time ORDER BY i.start_time;
SELECT COUNT(*) runs FROM calc.CalculationRun WHERE StartedAt >= DATEADD(hour,-6,SYSUTCDATETIME());

-- (2) Top statements in a window by CPU and log (trace share, HSE400 loader 4794, staleness map).
SELECT TOP 15 p.query_id, SUM(rs.count_executions) execs,
  CAST(SUM(rs.avg_cpu_time*rs.count_executions)/1e6 AS decimal(12,1)) cpu_s,
  CAST(SUM(rs.avg_log_bytes_used*rs.count_executions)/1048576 AS decimal(12,1)) log_mb,
  LEFT(qt.query_sql_text, 120) txt
FROM sys.query_store_runtime_stats rs
JOIN sys.query_store_runtime_stats_interval i ON i.runtime_stats_interval_id = rs.runtime_stats_interval_id
JOIN sys.query_store_plan p ON p.plan_id = rs.plan_id
JOIN sys.query_store_query q ON q.query_id = p.query_id
JOIN sys.query_store_query_text qt ON qt.query_text_id = q.query_text_id
WHERE i.start_time >= DATEADD(hour,-2,SYSUTCDATETIME())
GROUP BY p.query_id, qt.query_sql_text ORDER BY cpu_s DESC;

-- (3) Queue waits and run times by job type and lane (PERF-01/04/13). Wait = CreatedAt→StartedAt.
SELECT RIGHT(JobCode,40) code, Lane, State, COUNT(*) n,
  AVG(DATEDIFF(millisecond, CreatedAt, StartedAt)/1000.0) avg_wait_s,
  MAX(DATEDIFF(millisecond, CreatedAt, StartedAt)/1000.0) max_wait_s,
  AVG(DATEDIFF(millisecond, StartedAt, UpdatedAt)/1000.0) avg_span_s
FROM itg.JobProgress WHERE CreatedAt >= DATEADD(hour,-2,SYSUTCDATETIME())
GROUP BY RIGHT(JobCode,40), Lane, State ORDER BY n DESC;

-- (4) Live queue depth and Running count per lane (run every 15 s during the load test).
SELECT Lane, State, COUNT(*) n, MIN(AvailableAt) oldest
FROM itg.JobProgress WITH (INDEX(IX_JobProgress_Claim))
WHERE Lane IS NOT NULL AND State IN ('Queued','Running') GROUP BY Lane, State;

-- (5) Chain progress and absorption (PERF-02): Cancelled-by-absorb vs Succeeded year chains.
SELECT TargetKey, State, COUNT(*) n, MAX(JSON_VALUE(Payload,'$.chainTotal')) total
FROM itg.JobProgress WHERE TargetKey LIKE '%-y%' AND CreatedAt >= DATEADD(hour,-4,SYSUTCDATETIME())
GROUP BY TargetKey, State ORDER BY TargetKey;

-- (6) Server pressure deltas (snapshot before/after; PERF-05). Instance-level, read-only.
SELECT wait_type, waiting_tasks_count, wait_time_ms, max_wait_time_ms FROM sys.dm_os_wait_stats
WHERE wait_type IN ('THREADPOOL','RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE','RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE_QUERY_COMPILE','WRITELOG',
                    'PAGEIOLATCH_SH','LCK_M_IX','LCK_M_X','LCK_M_S','CXCONSUMER','SOS_SCHEDULER_YIELD');
SELECT COUNT(*) workers, SUM(CASE WHEN state='RUNNING' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) running FROM sys.dm_os_workers;
SELECT scheduler_id, current_tasks_count, runnable_tasks_count, active_workers_count, work_queue_count
FROM sys.dm_os_schedulers WHERE status = 'VISIBLE ONLINE';
SELECT pool_id, grantee_count, waiter_count, available_memory_kb/1024 avail_mb FROM sys.dm_exec_query_resource_semaphores;

-- (7) Who is heavy right now (program name from PSS-03 Application Name).
SELECT s.program_name, COUNT(*) req, SUM(r.cpu_time) cpu_ms, MAX(r.dop) max_dop,
  SUM(CASE WHEN r.wait_type LIKE 'LCK%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) blocked
FROM sys.dm_exec_requests r JOIN sys.dm_exec_sessions s ON s.session_id = r.session_id
WHERE s.is_user_process = 1 GROUP BY s.program_name;
SELECT g.session_id, s.program_name, g.requested_memory_kb/1024 req_mb, g.granted_memory_kb/1024 granted_mb, g.wait_time_ms
FROM sys.dm_exec_query_memory_grants g JOIN sys.dm_exec_sessions s ON s.session_id = g.session_id;

-- (8) Log and file IO delta (PERF-03): take before/after a single yearly run.
SELECT mf.type_desc, vfs.num_of_bytes_written/1048576 mb_written, vfs.io_stall_write_ms
FROM sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats(DB_ID(), NULL) vfs
JOIN sys.master_files mf ON mf.database_id = vfs.database_id AND mf.file_id = vfs.file_id;
SELECT cntr_value AS ple_s FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters
WHERE counter_name = 'Page life expectancy' AND object_name LIKE '%Buffer Manager%';

-- (9) Trace volume per run (PERF-03): rows of the last N Current runs.
SELECT TOP 10 r.Id, r.DocumentId, r.PeriodKey,
  (SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) FROM calc.CalculationStep s WITH (INDEX(IX_CalculationStep_Run)) WHERE s.CalculationRunId = r.Id) steps,
  (SELECT COUNT_BIG(*) FROM calc.CalculationResult x WITH (INDEX(IX_CalculationResult_Run)) WHERE x.CalculationRunId = r.Id) results
FROM calc.CalculationRun r WHERE r.Status = 'Current' AND r.DocumentId IS NOT NULL ORDER BY r.Id DESC;

-- (10) Role-assignment scans (PERF-14) and My-tasks index (PERF-15).
SELECT i.name, us.user_seeks, us.user_scans, us.user_lookups FROM sys.indexes i
LEFT JOIN sys.dm_db_index_usage_stats us ON us.object_id = i.object_id AND us.index_id = i.index_id AND us.database_id = DB_ID()
WHERE i.object_id IN (OBJECT_ID('sec.RoleAssignment'), OBJECT_ID('itg.JobProgress'));

-- (11) Staleness map after deploying HEAD: no flat-form executions; tagged full or delta only.
SELECT TOP 10 q.query_id, SUM(rs.count_executions) execs,
  CAST(SUM(rs.avg_cpu_time*rs.count_executions)/SUM(rs.count_executions)/1000 AS decimal(10,1)) avg_cpu_ms,
  MAX(rs.last_execution_time) last_exec, LEFT(qt.query_sql_text, 100) txt
FROM sys.query_store_query q
JOIN sys.query_store_query_text qt ON qt.query_text_id = q.query_text_id
JOIN sys.query_store_plan p ON p.query_id = q.query_id
JOIN sys.query_store_runtime_stats rs ON rs.plan_id = p.plan_id
WHERE qt.query_sql_text LIKE '%MIN(t.At) AS Since%' OR qt.query_sql_text LIKE '%StaleMap:%'
GROUP BY q.query_id, qt.query_sql_text ORDER BY last_exec DESC;
```

### 5.2 Load-test scenario (k6 or NBomber)

**Rig:**
- Customer-like hardware: SQL 20 cores / 32 GB with MAXDOP 4 and cost threshold 50; app server 24 cores / 32 GB.
- Database (Worker) mode with `ECR_Jobs__Queue__Mode=Database` and `ECR_Jobs__Recalculation__Executor=Worker`.
- A Land copy scaled to ≥ 100 documents (clone documents across projects).
- Telemetry on (`Telemetry:Enabled=true`, OTLP) and `Application Name` visible.

**Sign-in:**
- Pre-create 1000 local test users (seed file) or use Kerberos test accounts.
- **Phase 0 (sign-in burst):** 1000 virtual users sign in over 5 min from **one source address**, and separately from 50 addresses. Expect 0 × 429 after the PERF-07 fix. Today at most 60 per minute pass, so at most 300 in 5 minutes, and ≥ 700 users get at least one 429.

**Virtual users, steady state 60 min after a 10-min ramp:**

| Profile | Count | Behaviour | Think time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Viewer | 600 | Open document (all GETs the page makes), then loop the client pollers: `jobs?mine` 30 s, `sheets/{id}/changes` 30 s, `discussions/summary` 32 s; every 5 min switch sheet (slice GETs for visible tables). | Exponential, mean 30 s between actions |
| Editor | 300 | Same as viewer, plus `PATCH /documents/{id}/cells` with 1–5 cells every 5 s for 2 min, pause 3 min, repeat. Follow `recalculationJobId` at 2 s until final, then refetch 3 slices. | As stated |
| Recalculator | 100 (subset of editors) | `POST …/recalculate` once per 20 min per user, random month; follow at 1.5 s plus `jobs?mine` at 3 s while Queued or Running, as the client does. | 20 min |
| HSE400 editor | 1 | PATCH the HSE400 source every 60 s (PERF-06). | 60 s |
| Admin | 2 | Jobs page (`jobs/summary` 10 s), health page. | — |

**Pass criteria (NFR):**
- Document `GET` p95 < 3 s.
- PATCH p95 < 1 s.
- Formula job `CreatedAt→StartedAt` p95 < 10 s (ФВ-12.2).
- Manual recalculation start p95 < agreed SLA (proposal: 2 min).
- 0 THREADPOOL waits.
- RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE delta ≈ 0.
- No HTTP 5xx and no `databaseBusy`.
- Log write rate below the device's sustained throughput.

**Record each run:** §5.1 queries (1), (3), (4) and (6) every 15 min; (8) before and after; API `dotnet-counters` (`System.Runtime`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting`, connection-pool counters `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EventSource`).

**A/B order:**
1. Baseline (HEAD).
2. With PERF-05 cap.
3. Plus PERF-01/02.
4. Plus PERF-03(b).
5. Plus PERF-04 config. Report wait distributions per step.

## 6. Рішення людини (21.11.2026, вечір)

1. **PERF-01/02 — прийнято «лише змінені місяці».** Ручне «Перерахувати» на документі з річною розкладкою рахує лише місяці, де змінилися входи (детектор D-562 `NightlyInputChangeQuery` на рівні документ × місяць) + завжди місяць на екрані; нове натискання під час ланцюжка НЕ скидає його на січень, а дописує лише ті вже пораховані місяці, чиї входи змінились після їхнього кроку. «Повний перерахунок» лишається для права `Calculation.Recalculate`. (Змінює B59, розширює D-562; читання H1 — «перерахувати лише змінені зроблені місяці».)
2. **PERF-03 — трасування:** (а) коли трасування пишеться — bulk-copy замість ~715 запитів EF, `TraceJson` стиснутий, доступ до кроків для людини без змін; (б) **у методології прапор «трасування»: за замовчуванням ВИМКНЕНО**, вмикають, коли треба подивитися проміжні розрахунки. (Змінює ЗБР-1 / D-560 — трасування не для кожного прогону.)
3. **PERF-05/10 — прийнято «глобальна стеля + чесність»:** одна стеля на всі важкі перерахунки (ручні, авто, каскадні, діти розкладу; типово від ядер SQL, налаштовувана), рекомендований MAXDOP у документації; черга чергує користувачів (один користувач не займає всю чергу); користувач бачить позицію в черзі й орієнтовний час.
4. **PERF-12 — прийнято «воркер обов'язковий у продакшені»:** у Production типовий режим — черга в базі + служба EcrWorker; Quartz у API — лише dev/малі інсталяції (попередження на старті).
5. **PERF-06 (каскад HSE400 лише по змінених місяцях) і PERF-07 (окрема межа Windows-входу / X-Forwarded-For) — НЕ обрано**: без змін, доки людина не вирішить інакше.
6. Без рішення людини (виконуються): PERF-08/09/16 (клієнт, лан `perf-client` — готово), PERF-11/13/14/15/17/18 (лан `perf-server-small`), PERF-04 — конфіг/документація разом із п. 3.
7. **(21.11, після perf-trace) Трасування вимкнене за замовчуванням — прийнято як є.** При помилках розрахунку користувачі вмикають трасування й діагностують. **Головна вимога людини: під час діагностики система має допомагати знайти, де проблема** — помилка розрахунку (StepError) у панелі проблем має вести до діагностики: пояснити, що трасування вимкнене, хто/де його вмикає (посилання на методологію), і що після перерахунку буде видно проблемний крок; з увімкненим трасуванням — показувати збійний крок і його входи. → доробка в лані perf-trace після рев'ю.
8. **(22.11) PERF-06 — ПРИЙНЯТО:** правка документа-джерела HSE400 перераховує у споживачів ЛИШЕ місяці, яких правка реально стосується, і кілька правок у коротке вікно об'єднуються в один перерахунок. Людина: від HSE400 залежить ~200 документів на рік. **PERF-07 — ПРИЙНЯТО «зробити зараз»:** окрема (вища) межа для Windows-входу; довіра X-Forwarded-For від відомих проксі (налаштування) — задокументувати й перевірити.
